agent_notes: Diff only adds sanitize_log_value() around three log.debug() interpolation sites in src/python/model/model.py (add_file, remove_file, update_file) — a security-tightening change closing a CWE-117 log injection vector (CRLF/ANSI log forging via file.name or filename). Verified sanitize_log_value in src/python/common/types.py correctly escapes CR/LF and C0 control chars/DEL; no bypass found in the hunk. No new vulnerability introduced.

This change follows the codebase's established pattern. `sanitize_log_value` is the project's helper for stopping log injection (CWE-117). It is defined in src/python/common/types.py, exported from src/python/common/__init__.py, and already used in src/python/lftp/lftp.py, src/python/lftp/job_status_parser.py, src/python/controller/controller.py, src/python/controller/webhook_manager.py and src/python/controller/scan/remote_scanner.py. That is 56 occurrences across 12 files, counting tests. The diff applies the same helper the same way: it wraps the interpolated value inside the existing `.format()` call.

No new dependency or import cycle. model/model.py already imported from `common` (AppError), so adding a second name to that import creates no new edge. common/types.py imports only the stdlib `inspect`, and nothing under src/python/common imports `model` (encryption.py merely contains the word 'model' and has no import of it). There is no back-edge.
No reach into private internals of another module. The helper comes from `common`'s public package surface, not a deep path to `common.types`, which matches how controller.py and lftp.py import it.

All three log sites in model.py that interpolate a value derived from a filename (add, remove and update file) are now sanitized. The other logger calls in model.py (lines 61, 70 and 73) log only fixed strings, so the file is now fully covered for this concern.

The exception messages raised in these same methods ('File already exists in the model' and similar) do not interpolate the filename, so no unsanitized copy of the value escapes through ModelError. This is consistent with the scope of the change.

There are 11 importers of model.py (controller/*, web/handler/stream_model.py, web/serialize/serialize_model.py, model/diff.py and others). None of them are affected: the change only alters debug log text and leaves Model's public API, its return values and the stored file names untouched. sanitize_log_value is applied only to the logged copy of the value, never to the dictionary key.

This commit appears to be the GREEN step following RED commit 7035477, which added failing sanitization tests for these model log sites (in src/python/tests/unittests/test_model/test_model.py, per the related-files listing). That matches the RED/GREEN cadence used for the earlier controller.py log sites (3c1b631 → 45ff4bd).

agent_notes: Change class: this tightens a control. It wraps three DEBUG log sites in Model.add_file, Model.remove_file and Model.update_file (src/python/model/model.py:81, 97, 112) with the existing `sanitize_log_value` helper from src/python/common/types.py:17, to prevent CWE-117 log injection.
Public API: unchanged. The method signatures, return values, exceptions raised (ModelError) and the order of state changes are all the same. Only the text passed to logger.debug changes.

What breaks if this has a bug: the sanitizer runs before the `ModelError` membership checks. If it raised, add, remove and update in the model would all fail. That would stop the controller's model-diff loop, and with it the web stream/serialize and auto_queue. I checked the helper: it only calls `str.replace` and `ord` on a str. `ModelFile.name` is a str, and the only production caller of `remove_file` (controller.py:589) passes `diff.old_file.name`, also a str. No crash path was found.

Behavior change: only the content of DEBUG log lines changes. Filenames containing control characters, CR/LF or DEL now appear as \r, \n or \xHH escapes. Anything that greps logs for raw filenames with control characters would see different text. That is the intended effect, and it only matters for unusual names.
C1 control characters (0x80-0x9F) are left unescaped by design (types.py:28-31). That gap was already in the helper before this diff, so it is not introduced here.
Database, schema or migration impact: none.
Blast radius: one module (model.py) changes, with 11 importers, but none of them depend on the log text. User-visible impact is limited to how DEBUG-level log lines look.
Verdict: shippable as-is. The only finding is a non-blocking perf note.

findings.fix_hint: Optionally use lazy logging (`self.logger.debug("... '%s'", sanitize_log_value(...))` still evaluates eagerly), so gate with `if self.logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)` if profiling shows cost
findings.problem: The log message is built with an eager `.format()`, so `sanitize_log_value` runs even when DEBUG is disabled. The sanitizer loops over the filename one character at a time in pure Python (src/python/common/types.py:52-57). `update_file` runs for each changed file on every model-diff cycle (controller.py around line 589 drives add/remove/update), so this adds an O(len(name)) loop per file per scan. pending: profile a scan cycle with a large remote listing (thousands of entries) to see whether this cost is measurable. With typical filename lengths of about 100 characters it is very likely negligible.
findings.title: Sanitizer runs on every add/update even when DEBUG logging is off
findings.why_it_matters: This runs on the hot path of model updates. The cost is small per call but repeats on every scan cycle. It is a tech-debt or perf note, not a correctness issue.
